channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Jollibee’s Global IPO Can Wait
item.description: Jollibee plans to spin off its fast-growing international business and list it in Hong Kong. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Juliana Liu says the split makes sense, but the overseas operation needs at least another year to prove it can stand on its own. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: French Conservatives to Keep Senate Majority as Far Right Gains
item.description: France’s conservative Republicans party and its allies were set to retain a majority in the Senate, even as the populist National Rally gained several seats and boosted its position in the upper house.
item.dc:creator: Alan Katz and Samy Adghirni

item.title: Labour's Douglas Alexander welcomes social care reform
item.description: UK Secretary of State for Scotland Douglas Alexander spoke to Bloomberg TV at the annual Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, saying that "there's a recognition that we face big constraints and big structural challenges" but that he personally welcomes Burnham's plans around social care. He also commented on the UK's relationship with the US in light of the RAF Fairford incident in the UK, saying he assures that the intelligence sharing relationships between the US, US, and allies across the West "is as strong as it's ever been". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Policy on Taiwan Is Unchanged After Xi’s Visit, Perdue Says
item.description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping discuss Taiwan arms sales every time they get together but the American stance on the self-ruled island remains unchanged following the Chinese leader’s state visit to Washington last week, the US president’s top envoy to Beijing said.
item.dc:creator: Phila Siu

item.title: Trump Says He Expects Renewed Iran Talks This Week, Axios Says
item.description: President Donald Trump said he expects talks with Iran to resume this week, even after rejecting the latest Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Axios reported, citing a phone interview with the president.
item.dc:creator: Tony Czuczka

item.title: Trump Says Suspects Arrested in UK Had Been Under Surveillance
item.description: President Donald Trump said that some of the men arrested Sunday on terrorism charges by the UK near an air base used by the US military were under surveillance and aimed to inflict major damage.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Midterm Fight Expands Into Republican Strongholds
item.description: Puck News Washington writer Abby Livingston and Rutgers Eagleton Poll director Ashley Koning are on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss polling that shows Democrats gaining ground ahead of the midterms, including in traditionally Republican states and districts. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, they examine how economic concerns, farm policy and attitudes toward President Donald Trump are shaping races including the closely contested Texas Senate campaign. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Slovakia’s Fico Warns of Snap Vote as Coalition Majority at Risk
item.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said elections may be held as soon as January, as infighting between members of his ruling coalition threaten to cost him a majority in parliament.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Hornak

item.title: Burnham Faces First Labour Conference as PM
item.description: Bloomberg Daybreak Europe anchor Caroline Hepker is on Bloomberg This Weekend previewing Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s first Labour Party conference as leader, where his plans for social care, housing and other reforms face the constraints of a difficult UK fiscal outlook. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini from Liverpool, Hepker says Burnham has ruled out an early election as his government prepares for a challenging budget and tries to build on an initial increase in confidence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US China Trade Truce Leaves Key Issues Unresolved
item.description: Bloomberg News Washington Bureau Chief Peggy Collins is on Bloomberg This Weekend discussing stalled US-Iran negotiations, President Donald Trump’s summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and the continuing dispute over White House press access. She tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that the US-China summit extended the trade truce through Jan. 10 but left major trade and AI questions unresolved, while political and cost-of-living pressures are intensifying ahead of the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Conducts Air-Sea Exercise Near Scarborough Shoal on Sunday
item.description: China‘s People’s Liberation Army Southern Theater Command conducted a joint naval and air training exercise in the waters and airspace around Scarborough Shoal on Sept. 27.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Swiss Reject Stricter Neutrality, Preserving Government Leeway
item.description: Swiss voters rejected a bid to enshrine stricter neutrality in the constitution, preserving the government’s freedom to interpret the doctrine flexibly and maintain sanctions against Russia.
item.dc:creator: Bastian Benrath-Wright

item.title: Russia Hits Ukraine Data Centers in Barrage That Killed Six
item.description: Russian airstrikes overnight and early Sunday killed at least six people across Ukraine and targeted a number of major data centers in Kyiv, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Burnham Draws Backlash With Cool Response to Heathrow Expansion
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s suggestion that he could block plans for a third runway at Heathrow Airport set up a dispute with influential Labour interest groups just as the governing party’s annual conference got underway.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Joe Mayes

item.title: Turkey’s Ruling-Party Deputy Chair Resigns Amid Allegations Over Fund Crisis
item.description: Turkey’s widening fund crisis reached the ruling AK Party’s leadership, with Deputy Chair Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya stepping down from her party post after opposition allegations about stock trades involving her and her husband.
item.dc:creator: Ugur Yilmaz

item.title: Burnham Hints at New UK Taxes to Fund Major Reform to Elder Care
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham displayed a willingness to take on one of the toughest policy traps in British policies by pledging to overhaul care for the elderly. He also indicated he may introduce new taxes to pay for it.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain and Alex Wickham

item.title: 5 Men Arrested Near UK’s RAF Fairford Base Used for Iran Strikes
item.description: UK police were investigating a potential terrorism incident after five men were arrested near an air base used in US strikes on Iran, with President Donald Trump saying the suspects were “looking to do big damage” to the facility.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham and Angela Cullen

item.title: Iran Says Won’t Soften Demands as Trump Rejects Hormuz Offer
item.description: Iran stuck to its seven-day proposal for reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz, saying it won’t soften its conditions, while President Donald Trump sent mixed signals about his willingness to reach a deal.
item.dc:creator: Eltaf Najafizada and Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Kazakh President Fires Defense Minister After Drill Deaths
item.description: Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev dismissed his defense minister after 14 military personnel died during exercises in the Caspian Sea.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Serb President Vucic to Quit in Switch to PM Post, Echoing Putin’s Power Move
item.description: Embattled Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic resigned on Sunday in a well-telegraphed move as he seeks to transition to the role of prime minister as a way of staying close to power in the Balkan nation.
item.dc:creator: Jasmina Kuzmanovic and Jan Bratanic
